text:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach detected in eu-west for inference-service (route: /v1/generate). SLO burn 47% over the last 5m. PagerDuty incident created: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident INC12345 triggered and notified the on-call rotation.

Alex: acked. I'm taking this. Seeing p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1.9s. Thanks for the notification.

Sam: thx Alex. Any customer visible errors?

Alex: No 5xx spike, just long tail. Traces show a small subset of requests hitting long KV cache warmups and sidecar queueing.

Liz: @Alex can you confirm if this correlates with the batcher throttling we pushed in the autoscaler change last night?

Alex: checking now — staging autoscale config rolled to prod at 02:12 UTC (PR #842). I see increased batching for long-seq requests. Could be interaction with GPU sidecar eviction.

Priya: customer-jobs queue shows higher average seq_len for eu-west. Might be a traffic shift from APAC -> EU.

product-jane: we had a contract @BigRetail running large batched jobs in eu-west during the promotion window. They might be the spike.

Alex: ok plan: 1) temporarily reduce max_batch_size to 8 for the model pool in eu-west 2) enable KV cache sticky routing for hot keys 3) if that doesn't help, fallback route to smaller-quantized variant (model-xq).

Sam: @Alex quick note — that config change will roll across 3 nodes, suggest canary to one node first. Do we want to canary or emergency-roll?

Alex: canary one node first (node-eu-3), monitor p99 for 2 minutes, then roll remainder if improvement.

Liz: while Alex is canarying, I'll add a temporary routing rule in the smart-router to divert 20% of new sessions to eu-west-fallback region (eu-central) to ease tail latency.

Priya: started dumping a sample of slow request traces to /tmp/slow-traces-INC12345.log, uploading to the incident artifacts bucket now. Link: https://s3.example/incident/INC12345/slow-traces.log

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary config applied to node-eu-3: set max_batch_size=8.

Alex: canary complete. p99 dropped from 1.9s -> 1.1s on node-eu-3 within 90s. Good signal.

Sam: routing diversion in place. Observability shows overall p99 for eu-west trending down to 1.2s. still above SLO but improving.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident INC12345 acknowledged by Alex at 1788881240.

Alex: rolling config to remaining nodes. ETA ~ 3m. continuing to watch slow traces.

Liz: noted customer impact: BigRetail reported delayed responses but no failed requests. CS notified and triaging communications.

product-jane: pls keep me posted — if fallback region impacts model freshness, we need to coordinate with them.

Priya: KV cache hits on affected keys increased after canary, looks like sticky policy helped.

Alex: full roll complete. eu-west p95 now 210ms, p99 680ms. SLO burn dropped to 4% over 5m.

Sam: nice work. Recommend we keep reduced batch size for next 6h and then investigate the autoscale heuristic interaction.

Liz: filing follow-up action: investigate autoscaler/batcher interaction, add a regression test for traffic-shift scenarios, and consider per-customer session-length routing.

Alex: will create the post-incident ticket and link traces/artifacts. For now I'm closing the PagerDuty incident.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident INC12345 resolved by Alex at 1788881350.

incident-bot: Incident resolved. Postmortem owner: Alex. Action items assigned: #INC-A1 (autoscaler regression), #INC-A2 (routing policy), #INC-A3 (customer comms).

product-jane: thanks all. Good faster mitigation steps — can we add a runbook snippet for this specific symptom?

Alex: yes, adding runbook snippet to the incident doc: ```
If p99 latency spike without 5xx and traces show KV warmups + increased seq_len:
  - Canary reduce max_batch_size to 8 on one node
  - If p99 improves, roll to all nodes
  - Divert 10-20% traffic to fallback region
  - Consider fallback to quantized model if capacity constrained
```

Sam: leaving a :thumbsup: reaction and handoff to Alex for the writeup.

Liz: closing thread here. Thanks everyone. :party_parrot:
